gap: No result ChatGPT got states how far the GardePro Link 1.0 hub actually reached in a named reviewer's woods test. MountainBuck (Dwayne) got a stable link at about 792 ft and at 540 ft up a steep wooded slope, and lost the link entirely at 1,300 ft. That is well short of the 1,600 ft 'typical' figure Magnolia repeats.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages. Magnolia Trail Camera (cited) gives only GardePro's claim of 'about 1,600 feet in typical use' and Gear Diary's '22 feet' motion detection. Its author says the Link is 'a research pick; I haven't run one.' The GardePro E8 3.0 Pro overview (cited) gives only the claimed 165 ft for direct phone connection, 0.1 s trigger and 7,800 mAh, with no measured figures. The E9 3.0 Pro page (cited) returned HTTP 429 to me, and GardePro's E9 overview doc has the same claims and no measurements. None of the three has a reviewer's pass/fail distances for the hub in woods or through walls, or a measured detection cutoff in yards.
decides: This confirms the Link 1.0 for the 'over 150 feet' branch ChatGPT asked about. Named tests show it connected at 400 ft through house walls and trees (MyBackyardBirding), at about 792 ft in woods and at about 950 yd in an open drive-away test (MountainBuck and Nate). It also limits the pick: in dense timber, plan for under about 800 ft, because MountainBuck failed at 1,300 ft and GardePro's own dense-forest figure is 384 ft. For the E8 and E9 3.0 Pro home-Wi-Fi cameras, no named reviewer has published a distance from the router. Their reach is whatever your 2.4 GHz router covers, so the E8 pick still rests only on maker specs.

findings.label: Hub-to-camera link, wooded terrain (MountainBuck)
findings.value: Connected at 540 ft on a steep, tree-dense slope. Stable at about 792 ft. No connection at 1,300 ft (0.25 mi).
findings.source_title: This Trail Cam System is Different — No Fees, Up to 16 Cameras & 3,000ft WiFi Range
findings.note: Test by YouTuber @MountainBuck (Dwayne). The page is GardePro's own summary of his video, published 2026-06-01. Result was recorded only as connected or not; no dBm.

findings.label: Motion detection cutoff (MountainBuck)
findings.value: Detected at 20 yd (60 ft), missed at 25 yd (75 ft)
findings.source_title: This Trail Cam System is Different — No Fees, Up to 16 Cameras & 3,000ft WiFi Range
findings.note: Side PIR sensors were off. Same video summary, dated 2026-06-01. Magnolia cites Gear Diary at 'about 22 feet' against a 'claimed 90', so the two reviewers' results differ a lot.

findings.label: Solar-backed battery in snow (MountainBuck)
findings.value: Battery still at 100% after 2 weeks and 288 photos plus 288 30-second videos
findings.source_title: This Trail Cam System is Different — No Fees, Up to 16 Cameras & 3,000ft WiFi Range

findings.label: Maximum hub-to-camera distance, drive-away test (Nate)
findings.value: About 950 yd (about 2,850 ft) with 2 bars. Triggered, took a photo and started a live stream at 6% battery. He expects 600-700 yd in dense woods.

findings.note: Test by @nateinthegreatoutdoors, with the camera on a truck driven away from the hub. GardePro summary dated 2026-05-19. Conversion: 950 yd × 3 = 2,850 ft. The 600-700 yd woods figure is his estimate, not a measurement.

findings.label: Winter battery without solar (Nate)

findings.source_title: link 1 0 no subscription trail cam nateinthegreatoutdoors review
findings.note: Clips set to 40-50 s to save power. GardePro summary dated 2026-05-19.

findings.label: Link from an indoor hub through walls and trees (MyBackyardBirding)

findings.label: Maker field test by terrain, stock 2 dB antenna
findings.value: Open flat 3,280 ft. Indoor hub across grassland 2,034 ft. Across a lake 1,168 ft. Sparse timber 885 ft. Through buildings 597 ft. Dense forest 384 ft.

findings.note: Measured by GardePro's engineering team, so these are maker figures, not independent. Mounted at 1.5 m. Published 2026-03-13. The page footnote mixes internal tests with 'verified user data'.
